original.prompt: Consider the following statements about US tariffs affecting India, as of May 2026:
items: After the US Supreme Court scrapped the "Liberation Day" tariffs, Washington imposed a 10% flat duty under Section 122.
The US Court of International Trade declared the 10% flat duties unlawful.
Following the US Court of International Trade ruling, US Customs stopped collecting the 10% duty from all importers.
original.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
original.explain: Statement 3 is wrong because US Customs continues to collect the 10% duty from everyone except the specific plaintiffs, so the court win is narrow. The Supreme Court's removal of the Liberation Day tariffs knocked out the original basis for the India-US trade deal and stalled negotiations.
original.source: US Customs continues to collect the tax from everyone except the specific plaintiffs.

rewritten.prompt: Consider the following statements about US tariffs affecting India, as of May 2026:
items: After the US Supreme Court scrapped the "Liberation Day" tariffs, Washington imposed a 10% flat duty under Section 301.
The US Court of International Trade declared the 10% flat duties unlawful.
Following the US Court of International Trade ruling, US Customs continued to collect the 10% duty from everyone except the specific plaintiffs.
rewritten.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
rewritten.explain: Statement 1 is wrong because the 10% flat duty was imposed under Section 122, while Section 301 was used to launch investigations into Indian trade practices. Statements 2 and 3 are correct, as the Court of International Trade's win against the duties was narrow and benefited only the plaintiffs.
rewritten.source: Washington pivoted to a 10% flat duty under Section 122 and launched Section 301 investigations into Indian trade practices (we covered it here).
